I had two big presentations due the same week.
One was for our actual client.
The other was just a rough, half-joking draft I'd made for my team, full of terrible jokes about our own department.
Both files had almost identical names, saved in the same folder.
Apparently past me thought that was a completely reasonable naming system.
Something like "deck_final" and "deck_final_v2," names that meant absolutely nothing helpful in the moment.
I got to the client meeting a few minutes early.
I plugged in my laptop, pulled up what I thought was the polished deck, and confidently clicked to the first slide in front of the whole room.

The title slide read, in giant letters, "Why Our Department Is Basically Held Together With Tape." Right behind it came a slide full of memes I'd made specifically to make my coworkers laugh during a boring Friday afternoon.
For a solid three seconds, absolutely nobody said anything.
I just stood there, clicker in hand, watching a room full of very serious clients stare at a slide about office chaos and broken printers.
I fumbled to close it and mumbled something about technical difficulties.
My face got hotter with every second it took my laptop to load the actual, correct file.
Somewhere behind me, someone quietly cleared their throat.
Once I finally pulled up the right deck, I tried to just barrel through the presentation like nothing had happened.
My voice was noticeably shakier than usual for at least the first ten minutes.
Nobody in the room said a word about it, which somehow made the silence feel even louder.
Afterward, one of the clients actually pulled me aside, laughing.
She said the tape slide was honestly the most memorable part of the whole meeting.
That somehow made me feel both mortified and a little relieved.
She even asked if she could get a copy of it for her own team.
She joked that half her department needed to see that exact printer meme.
Honestly, the whole disaster turned into a strangely good icebreaker for future meetings.
Now I rename every single file the second I finish making it.
Nothing vague.
Nothing that could ever get confused with a joke deck again.
My department really is held together with tape, professionally speaking, and apparently now everyone knows it.
I also created a separate folder just for internal jokes, clearly labeled in giant letters.
That way future me never has to relive those three horrifying seconds of watching clients read a slide about a broken office printer.
My coworker still asks, every single time we prep for a client meeting, whether I've triple-checked which file I'm opening.
